cues: Encapsulation wraps data and its functions into one unit, the class.
Private members can be used only inside the class.
Protected members are also visible to derived classes.
Public members form the interface everyone can use.
Outside code reaches only the public part.
text: Encapsulation wraps data and its functions into one unit, the class. The result is data hiding. Private members can be used only inside the class. Protected members are also visible to derived classes. Public members form the interface everyone can use. Outside code reaches only the public part.
